speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with hematuria and right flank pain; to help me pinpoint the cause, have you noticed any fever, chills, or nausea accompanying these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that information. Given your history of recurrent urinary tract infections and the presence of blood in your urine, have you noticed any blood clots, and have you experienced any episodes of fever or chills specifically during those past infections?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy; REQUEST TEST: Renal_ultrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Appearance is reddish, WBC 10-20 /HPF, RBC too numerous to count, Nitrites negative, Leukocyte Esterase positive. Renal_ultrasound: Multiple cysts present in the collecting ducts of the medulla; no obstruction noted.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is an interesting history provided by your previous doctor. Given your recurrent UTIs and the suspicion of tuberculosis, did you ever experience night sweats, unexplained weight loss, or cough with blood?

REQUEST TEST: Urine_culture_and_sensitivity; REQUEST TEST: AFB_stain_and_culture; REQUEST IMAGES: CT_Kidney_with_contrast.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urine_culture_and_sensitivity: Pending results; AFB_stain_and_culture: Pending results; CT_Kidney_with_contrast: Pending results. Please note that previous imaging (Intravenous Pyelogram) showed multiple cysts present in the collecting ducts of the medulla with no obstruction noted. Previous Urinalysis showed reddish appearance, WBC 10-20 /HPF, RBC too numerous to count, Nitrites negative, and Leukocyte Esterase positive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The urinalysis shows significant microscopic hematuria with white blood cells but negative nitrites, suggesting sterile inflammation rather than a typical bacterial infection. The previous IVP finding of multiple cysts in the collecting ducts is a key clue. Did you ever experience a persistent, dull ache in your right flank, or does the pain worsen with movement? Additionally, have you noticed any changes in your urination habits, such as increased frequency or urgency, despite the negative nitrite result?

REQUEST TEST: Cystoscopy; REQUEST IMAGES: CT_Kidney_with_contrast.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Cystoscopy: Pending results; CT_Kidney_with_contrast: Pending results.

speaker: Doctor
text: The imaging for the CT scan and cystoscopy is currently pending. Based on the previous IVP finding of multiple cysts in the collecting ducts with sterile inflammation (negative nitrites), we are strongly suspecting Medullary Cystic Kidney Disease. Have you noticed any signs of chronic kidney disease, such as fatigue, generalized swelling, or a decrease in your urine output?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history except noted recurrent urinary tract infections. No history of renal dialysis or known genetic diseases. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works in an office setting.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Medullary Cystic Kidney Disease (MCKD). The combination of recurrent UTIs, sterile pyuria, and a history of collecting duct cysts on IVP, in the absence of smoking or genetic family history, points strongly to this condition. Given the current pending imaging and lack of confirmed chronic kidney failure symptoms, I will conclude the workup here.
